characters.name: God
aliases: the Judge of all the earth
characters.note: The creator God of Genesis, who speaks, walks in the garden, makes covenants and appears in visions; he is also depicted in the form of visiting men (the three men at Mamre are called Yahweh's visitors). Appears from the first chapter to the end, in heavens, gardens, dreams and visions.

characters.name: Adam
characters.note: The first man, formed from the dust of the ground and placed in Eden; father of Cain, Abel and Seth, dies at 930 years. Appears in chapters 2 to 5 (the genealogy in chapter 5 is a list only).

characters.name: Eve
characters.note: The first woman, made from Adam's rib, wife of Adam; tempted by the serpent in Eden and mother of Cain, Abel and Seth. Chapters 2 to 4.

characters.name: the serpent
characters.note: The subtle serpent of the garden who tempts the woman and is cursed by God; chapter 3 only.

characters.name: Cain
characters.note: Firstborn son of Adam and Eve, a tiller of the ground who kills his brother Abel; builds a city named for his son Enoch; chapter 4. Tubal Cain in 4:22 is a different, later descendant of Lamech.

characters.name: Abel
characters.note: Second son of Adam and Eve, a keeper of sheep, killed by his brother Cain; chapter 4.

characters.name: Seth
characters.note: Son of Adam and Eve born after Abel's death, father of Enosh; named in chapters 4 and 5.

characters.name: Enoch (son of Cain)
characters.note: Son of Cain, whose name is given to the city Cain builds; only named in chapter 4.

characters.name: Enoch (son of Jared)
characters.note: Seventh from Adam; walked with God for 300 years and was taken by God without dying; chapter 5 only.

characters.name: Lamech (son of Methuselah)
characters.note: Father of Noah, who names his son Noah in hope of comfort from the ground's curse; chapter 5. Different from Lamech son of Methuselah's descendant in chapter 4 (see lamech_of_cain).

characters.name: Lamech (descendant of Cain)
characters.note: Descendant of Cain with two wives, Adah and Zillah, who boasts of killing a man; father of Jabal, Jubal and Tubal Cain; chapter 4. Not the same as Lamech who fathered Noah in chapter 5.

characters.name: Noah
characters.note: A righteous man who builds the ship (ark) and survives the flood with his family and the animals; later plants a vineyard and is drunk; chapters 5 to 9.

characters.name: Shem
characters.note: Eldest son of Noah, who with Japheth covers their father's nakedness; ancestor of Abram's line (chapter 11); chapters 5 to 11.

characters.name: Ham
characters.note: Son of Noah and father of Canaan, who sees his father's nakedness and is cursed through Canaan; chapters 9 to 10.

characters.name: Japheth
characters.note: Son of Noah who with Shem covers their father; chapters 9 and 10.

characters.name: Nimrod
characters.note: A mighty hunter and founder of cities in Babel and Assyria, son of Cush; chapter 10 only.

characters.name: Terah
characters.note: Father of Abram, Nahor and Haran, who leaves Ur with his family for Canaan but dies in Haran; chapters 11 and 12 (early).

characters.name: Abram
characters.note: Son of Terah, called by God from Haran to Canaan; renamed Abraham in chapter 17 and father of Isaac and Ishmael; the main patriarch of Genesis 11 to 25, appearing in chapters 12 to 25.

characters.name: Sarai
characters.note: Wife of Abram and mother of Isaac, renamed Sarah in chapter 17; appears in chapters 11 to 23.

characters.name: Lot
characters.note: Son of Haran, nephew of Abram, who settles in Sodom; he and his two daughters escape its destruction; chapters 11 to 19.

characters.name: Lot's wife
characters.note: Wife of Lot, who looks back at Sodom's destruction and becomes a pillar of salt; chapter 19.

characters.name: Lot's daughters
aliases: the firstborn and the younger daughter of Lot
characters.note: Two unnamed daughters of Lot who lie with their father and bear Moab and Ben Ammi; chapter 19. Treat as a group on stage.

characters.name: Hagar
characters.note: Egyptian servant of Sarai, mother of Ishmael by Abram; flees to the wilderness and is comforted by an angel; chapters 16 and 21.

characters.name: Ishmael
characters.note: Son of Abram and Hagar, sent away with his mother; ancestor of the Ishmaelites; chapters 16, 17, 21, 25.

characters.name: Isaac
characters.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, born in old age; the promised heir; married to Rebekah; father of Esau and Jacob; chapters 17 to 35.

characters.name: Rebekah
characters.note: Wife of Isaac and mother of Esau and Jacob; daughter of Bethuel, sister of Laban; chapters 22 to 35.

characters.name: Abimelech (king of Gerar in Abraham's time)
characters.note: King of Gerar who takes Sarah into his household; chapters 20 and 21. The later Abimelech king of the Philistines in Isaac's time is a different individual, listed separately.

characters.name: Abimelech (Philistine king in Isaac's time)
characters.note: Philistine king of Gerar in Isaac's time who makes a covenant with Isaac; chapter 26. Different from the Abimelech of Abraham's time (chapters 20 and 21).

characters.name: Phicol
characters.note: Captain of the army of Abimelech who makes a covenant with Abraham, and later with Isaac; chapters 21 and 26.

characters.name: Eliezer of Damascus
aliases: the eldest servant of Abraham's house
characters.note: Abraham's servant who would have been his heir, and who is sent to find Isaac a wife (chapter 24, where he is unnamed). Listed here since he is named in 15:2 and the servant of chapter 24 is the same person.

characters.name: Bethuel
characters.note: Son of Nahor and Milcah, father of Rebekah and Laban; chapters 22 and 24.

characters.name: Laban
characters.note: Brother of Rebekah and father of Leah and Rachel; Jacob serves him; chapters 24, 27 to 31. Different from Laban the Syrian mentioned in 31:20 only by context, but the same individual.

characters.name: Esau
characters.note: Elder son of Isaac and Rebekah, a hunter, who sells his birthright and loses his blessing to Jacob; chapters 25 to 36.

characters.name: Jacob
characters.note: Younger son of Isaac and Rebekah, who wrestles with a man at Peniel and is renamed Israel; father of the twelve sons; chapters 25 to 50.

characters.name: Leah
characters.note: Elder daughter of Laban, first wife of Jacob, mother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, and others; chapters 29 to 35.

characters.name: Rachel
characters.note: Younger daughter of Laban, Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; chapters 29 to 35.

characters.name: Bilhah
characters.note: Servant of Rachel given to Jacob as a wife; mother of Dan and Naphtali; chapters 29, 30, 35.

characters.name: Zilpah
characters.note: Servant of Leah given to Jacob as a wife; mother of Gad and Asher; chapters 29, 30, 35.

characters.name: Reuben
characters.note: Firstborn son of Jacob and Leah; involved in the plot against Joseph and offers to save him; chapters 29, 35, 37, 42, 46, 49.

characters.name: Simeon
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; with Levi kills the men of Shechem; held hostage by Joseph in Egypt; chapters 29, 34, 42, 45.

characters.name: Levi
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; with Simeon avenges Dinah; chapters 29, 34, 49.

characters.name: Judah
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; urges selling Joseph to the Ishmaelites; later pledges himself for Benjamin; chapters 29, 37, 38, 43, 44, 46, 49.

characters.name: Issachar
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; named in the lists and in the blessing of Jacob; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Zebulun
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Leah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Dan (son of Jacob)
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Naphtali
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Bilhah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Gad
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Zilpah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Asher
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Zilpah; chapters 30, 35, 46, 49.

characters.name: Joseph
characters.note: Son of Jacob and Rachel, sold into Egypt by his brothers, later vizier to Pharaoh; chapters 30 and 37 to 50.

characters.name: Benjamin
characters.note: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, who dies in childbirth naming him; brother of Joseph; chapters 35, 42 to 46.

characters.name: Dinah
characters.note: Daughter of Jacob and Leah, defiled by Shechem and avenged by her brothers; chapter 34 (and listed in 30:21 and 46:15).

characters.name: Shechem
characters.note: Prince of Shechem son of Hamor, who defiles Dinah and asks to marry her; chapter 34.

characters.name: Hamor
characters.note: Father of Shechem and prince of the Hivites, who negotiates with Jacob's sons; chapter 34.

characters.name: Tamar
characters.note: Daughter-in-law of Judah, widow of Er and then of Onan, who tricks Judah into fathering Perez and Zerah; chapter 38.

characters.name: Judah's wife (Shua's daughter)
characters.note: Canaanite wife of Judah and mother of Er, Onan and Shelah; she dies in chapter 38 and is otherwise unnamed.

characters.name: Potiphar
characters.note: Egyptian officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard who buys Joseph and imprisons him; chapter 39.

characters.name: Potiphar's wife
characters.note: Wife of Potiphar who tries to seduce Joseph and accuses him falsely; chapter 39.

characters.name: the chief cup bearer
aliases: the butler of the king of Egypt
characters.note: Pharaoh's cup bearer imprisoned with Joseph, who forgets him and then recommends him to Pharaoh; chapters 40 and 41.

characters.name: the chief baker
characters.note: Pharaoh's baker imprisoned with the cup bearer, who is hanged; chapters 40 and 41.

characters.name: Pharaoh (in Joseph's time)
characters.note: The Pharaoh who dreams of cattle and grain, promotes Joseph, and receives Jacob's family; chapters 12 (earlier Pharaoh), 40 to 47. The Pharaoh of Abram's time in chapter 12 is a different, earlier king.

characters.name: Pharaoh (in Abram's time)
characters.note: The Pharaoh who takes Sarai into his house and is plagued; chapter 12 only. Different from the Pharaoh of Joseph's time.

characters.name: Asenath
characters.note: Daughter of Potiphera priest of On, wife of Joseph and mother of Manasseh and Ephraim; chapters 41 and 46.

characters.name: Manasseh
characters.note: Elder son of Joseph and Asenath, blessed by Jacob in chapter 48.

characters.name: Ephraim
characters.note: Younger son of Joseph and Asenath, given precedence by Jacob in chapter 48.

characters.name: Ben Ammi
characters.note: Son of Lot's younger daughter, father of the Ammonites; named only in chapter 19.

characters.name: Keturah
characters.note: Abraham's later wife who bears him six sons; chapter 25.

characters.name: Melchizedek
characters.note: King of Salem and priest of God Most High who blesses Abram with bread and wine; chapter 14.

characters.name: Amraphel
characters.note: One of the four kings who fight the kings of the Plain; chapter 14.

characters.name: Chedorlaomer
characters.note: King of Elam who leads the coalition against the cities of the plain and captures Lot; chapter 14.

characters.name: Bera
characters.note: King of Sodom who fights Chedorlaomer and offers Abram goods; chapter 14.

characters.name: the men of Sodom
characters.note: Crowd of Sodom's men who surround Lot's house and demand the visitors; chapter 19. Acts as one group.

characters.name: the two angels
aliases: the men who came to Lot
characters.note: Two angels who visit Lot in Sodom and lead him out before its destruction; chapter 19.

characters.name: the three men at Mamre
characters.note: Three travellers who visit Abraham by the oaks of Mamre and foretell Sarah's son; chapter 18.

characters.name: Ephron the Hittite
characters.note: Hittite owner of the field and cave of Machpelah sold to Abraham for a burial place; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.

characters.name: the children of Heth
characters.note: The Hittite people among whom Abraham seeks a burial place; they speak together in chapter 23. Acts as one group.

characters.name: the Ishmaelites
characters.note: Merchants and traders who buy Joseph from his brothers and carry him to Egypt; chapter 37. Acts as one group.

characters.name: Joseph's brothers
characters.note: The ten (later eleven) sons of Jacob who sell Joseph and later come to Egypt for grain; chapters 34, 37, 42 to 50. Acts as one group when on stage.

characters.name: the angels at the ladder
characters.note: Angels seen ascending and descending the stairway in Jacob's dream at Bethel; chapter 28.

characters.name: the man at Peniel
characters.note: The man who wrestles Jacob at the ford of the Jabbok, later understood as God; chapter 32.

locations.name: Eden
locations.note: The garden planted by God in the east, watered by four rivers, where Adam and Eve live; chapters 2 and 3.; garden of God; the tree of life and of knowledge grow in its middle.; chapters 2 to 3.

locations.name: Nod
locations.note: The land east of Eden where Cain goes after killing Abel and where he builds a city; chapter 4.; chapter 4.

locations.name: the mountains of Ararat
locations.note: The mountains where Noah's ship rests after the flood; chapter 8.; chapter 8.

locations.name: Babel
locations.note: Site of the tower built by mankind on the plain of Shinar, where the language is confused; chapter 11. Babel is also one of the first cities of Nimrod's kingdom (chapter 10).; chapters 10 and 11.

locations.name: Ur of the Chaldees
locations.note: City in Mesopotamia from which Terah leaves with Abram; chapters 11 and 15.; chapters 11, 15.

locations.name: Haran
locations.note: City in northern Mesopotamia where Terah settles and dies and where Abram stays for a time; chapters 11 and 12.; chapters 11 to 12.

locations.name: the land of Canaan
locations.note: The land God promises to Abram's offspring, where the patriarchs live; chapters 12 to 50.; chapters 12 to 50.

locations.name: Egypt
locations.note: The land Abram visits in famine (chapter 12) and where Joseph rises to rule and the family settles (chapters 37 to 50).; chapters 12, 37 to 50.

locations.name: Shechem
locations.note: City in Canaan where Jacob buys land and where Dinah is defiled; chapters 12, 33, 34, 35, 37.; chapters 12, 33, 34, 37.

locations.name: Bethel
locations.note: A place between Bethel and Ai where Abram builds an altar, and where Jacob sees the ladder and names the place Bethel; chapters 12, 13, 28, 31, 35.; chapters 12, 28, 35.

locations.name: Sodom
locations.note: Wicked city of the plain where Lot lives and which God destroys with Gomorrah; chapters 13, 14, 18, 19.; chapters 13, 18, 19.

locations.name: Gomorrah
locations.note: City of the plain destroyed with Sodom; chapters 13, 14, 18, 19.; chapters 13, 18, 19.

locations.name: the plain of the Jordan
locations.note: The well-watered plain where Lot chooses to live; chapter 13.; chapter 13.

locations.name: Hebron
locations.note: Place where Abram settles by the oaks of Mamre and where Sarah dies and is buried in the cave of Machpelah; chapters 13, 14, 18, 23, 35, 37.; chapters 13, 18, 23, 35, 37, 49, 50.

locations.name: Gerar
locations.note: Philistine town where Abraham and Isaac live as foreigners and where Abimelech rules; chapters 20 and 26.; chapters 20, 26.

locations.name: Beersheba
locations.note: A well and place where Abraham and Abimelech make a covenant and where Isaac builds an altar; chapters 21, 22, 26, 28, 46.; chapters 21, 22, 26, 28, 46.

locations.name: the land of Moriah
locations.note: Place where Abraham takes Isaac for the sacrifice; chapter 22.; chapter 22.

locations.name: Beer Lahai Roi
locations.note: The well where Hagar is comforted and where Isaac later lives; chapters 16, 24, 25.; chapters 16, 24, 25.

locations.name: Paddan Aram
locations.note: Region of Haran to which Jacob flees and where Laban lives and Jacob marries and has children; chapters 24, 25, 28, 29, 31, 35.; chapters 24, 28 to 31, 35.

locations.name: the ford of the Jabbok
locations.note: Place on the river where Jacob wrestles with the man and is renamed Israel; chapters 32, 33.; chapter 32.

locations.name: Succoth
locations.note: Place where Jacob builds a house and shelters for his livestock; chapter 33.; chapter 33.

locations.name: Dothan
locations.note: Place where Joseph's brothers find him and sell him; chapter 37.; chapter 37.

locations.name: Dan
locations.note: A place to which Abram pursues the kings of the east; chapter 14. The later tribe is named in chapter 49.; chapter 14.

locations.name: Goshen
locations.note: Region of Egypt where Jacob's family settles; chapters 45 to 50.; chapters 45 to 50.

locations.name: the pit in the wilderness
locations.note: The empty pit into which Joseph's brothers throw him; chapter 37.; chapter 37.

locations.name: the threshing floor of Atad
locations.note: Place beyond the Jordan where the funeral procession of Jacob mourns; chapter 50.; chapter 50.

locations.name: the cave of Machpelah
locations.note: The cave in the field of Machpelah before Mamre bought by Abraham as a burial place; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.; chapters 23, 25, 49, 50.

locations.name: the prison
aliases: the place where the king's prisoners were bound
locations.note: The Egyptian prison where Joseph is kept with Pharaoh's prisoners; chapters 39 to 41.; chapters 39 to 41.

locations.name: Pharaoh's house
locations.note: The royal house in Egypt where Joseph serves; chapters 12, 41, 45, 47.; chapters 12, 41, 45, 47.

brief.tone: Ancient, solemn and intimate: a primordial beginning followed by family dramas of blessing, betrayal, reconciliation and promise.
depiction_rules: God is not given a human face or body; show him by light, voice, a cloud or a hand where tradition permits, and angels as luminous messengers.
Show the tree of life and knowledge and the serpent with restraint; the serpent may be drawn as a plain animal.
Do not depict the nakedness of Noah, Ham, Lot or Lot's daughters explicitly; cover or turn figures away.
Lot's wife may be shown as a pillar of salt without gore.
Depict the flood, Sodom and the binding of Isaac with weight and dignity, without gratuitous violence.

era.name: The ancient Near East, from the primeval world through the patriarchal age to Egypt in the Middle or Late Bronze Age
era.people: Semitic herders, farmers and city dwellers of Mesopotamia, Canaan, and Egypt; Egyptians, Philistines, Hittites and Canaanites appear in the narrative. People have dark hair and beards for men and wear simple, earth-toned clothing.
era.dress: Simple linen or wool tunics and robes, cloaks and head coverings, sandals; Egyptian officials in fine linen with gold chains; women veiled in the presence of men.
era.buildings_and_objects: Mud-brick and stone cities such as Ur, tents of goat hair for nomads, altars of stone, wells, vineyards, flocks, camels and donkeys, chariots in Egypt.
era.technology: Bronze and early iron tools, pottery, weaving and the potter's wheel; no writing of the text itself at the time described, no firearms, no metal coins (silver is weighed by the shekel).
